# ASSESSMENT OF THE IMMUNOLOGICAL RESPONSE GENERATED BY A VACANE WATER-MANAGED BY THE STORAGE FOR CONTROL OF THE DISEASE OF NEWCASTLE

Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV) is a cause of respiratory diseases that cause significant economic losses to poultry producers. The vaccination in food has been efficient for disease control in traspatium birds; however, in Colombia the use of this strategy is poorly understood. In this study the viability of the strains VH and La Sota mixed with cooked rice, oiled raw rice and cooked corn was determined. The mixtures were inoculated in SPF eggs from 9 to 11 days of incubation. The viral title was determined and the viral load was determined by RT-qPCR. Subsequently, 160 chickens Babcock were randomly divided into four groups: negative control, ocular route, drinking water and maize. The birds were immunized at day 28 of age with the VH strain and were taken serums for immunohistochemical differences. The viral excretion and expression of IL-6 and IFN-¿, days 2 and 4 post-vaccination by RT-qPCR were quantified as the expression of the LH strain and were measured as the vaccine and the most common disease.
